x: The mantle is mostly solid but flows slowly over geological time, which drives convection. The outer core is liquid and the crust and inner core are rigid.
t: Discriminate the state of each layer.

x: Option C is incorrect: iron is about 5% and ranks fourth. Aluminium is third at 8.13%, after oxygen (46.60%) and silicon (27.72%).
t: Check the rank and figure of each element.

x: Both are true and R explains A: S-waves cannot pass through liquids, so they vanish at the liquid outer core.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: A is true: by composition Earth has crust, mantle and core. B is false because mechanical layers are lithosphere, asthenosphere, mesosphere, outer core and inner core.
t: Discriminate compositional from mechanical layers.

x: I, II and IV are correct: continental crust is thicker, while oceanic crust is basaltic, denser and richer in Fe–Mg. III is false because continental crust is generally older.
t: Discriminate continental from oceanic crust.
s:
With reference to continental and oceanic crust, consider the following statements:
I. Continental crust is thicker than oceanic crust.
II. Oceanic crust is mainly basaltic and has higher density.
III. Continental crust is generally younger than oceanic crust.
IV. Oceanic crust contains more Fe–Mg than continental crust.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The Moho separates crust and mantle, Gutenberg mantle and outer core, Lehmann the outer and inner core and Conrad the upper and lower continental crust, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the boundary each discontinuity marks.

x: Magma that reaches the surface is called lava.
t: Discriminate magma from lava.

x: Both are true and R explains A: the weak asthenosphere lets lithospheric plates glide, so mantle flow below can move them.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Option A is incorrect: S-waves travel only through solids and stop at liquids. P-waves arrive first, S-waves are shear waves and surface waves do most damage.
t: Check the medium each wave can cross.

x: P-waves are fastest, S-waves cannot pass liquids, surface waves are most destructive and the P-wave shadow zone is about 103°–142°, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the features of each seismic wave.

x: Both are true: convection of conducting fluid in the outer core generates the magnetic field, and changes in that flow are linked to field reversals.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The core begins at about 2,900 km depth, at the Gutenberg discontinuity. 410 and 660 km are mantle transition-zone boundaries.
t: Discriminate depth figures from other units.

x: I, II and III are correct: divergence adds crust, subduction recycles it and convergence builds mountains. IV is false because seafloor spreading creates new crust.
t: Discriminate creation from destruction of crust.
s:
Consider the following statements about internal structure and surface consequences:
I. Divergence adds new crust.
II. Subduction destroys or recycles crust.
III. Convergence is associated with mountains and subduction.
IV. Seafloor spreading destroys old crust.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The crust is outermost, the mantle below the crust, the outer core below the mantle and the inner core at the centre, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Arrange the layers from the surface inward.

x: All five are correct: the solid crust is led by oxygen, the mantle is Mg–Fe silicate, and the solid inner core of iron and nickel is the NIFE core.
t: Recall the composition of each layer.

x: Calcium is 3.63% (fifth), sodium 2.83% (sixth), potassium 2.59% (seventh) and magnesium 2.09% (eighth), giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the order of crustal elements.

x: Option B is incorrect: the outer core is liquid, which is why S-waves stop there. The inner core is solid and the core is mainly iron and nickel.
t: Discriminate the state of each layer.

x: Continental crust is mainly granite, less dense than oceanic crust, generally older and rich in silicon and aluminium, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the features of continental crust.

x: Both are true: continental crust forms the continents and oceanic crust the ocean floors.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the 2,900 km depth of the mantle base does not explain why the mantle sits between crust and core.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All four are correct: the mostly solid mantle includes the asthenosphere and drives plate tectonics, volcanism and endogenic activity.
t: Recall the role of the mantle.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The mantle is predominantly solid.
II. The asthenosphere is an important upper zone of the mantle.
III. The mantle plays a major role in plate tectonics.
IV. The mantle plays a major role in volcanism and endogenic activity.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The lithosphere is a rigid upper zone made of the crust and uppermost mantle; the asthenosphere is a weak, ductile zone in the upper mantle below it, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Discriminate lithosphere from asthenosphere.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Lithosphere — mechanical nature
 b. Asthenosphere — mechanical nature
 c. Lithosphere — made up of
 d. Asthenosphere — located in

List-II
 i. Upper mantle below the lithosphere
 ii. Rigid upper zone
 iii. Crust and uppermost mantle
 iv. Weak and ductile zone

x: The lithosphere is a strong shell broken into plates, the asthenosphere goes with mantle flow, the Moho separates crust and mantle, and the liquid outer core generates the magnetic field, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Place each layer or boundary by depth and property.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Lithosphere
 b. Asthenosphere
 c. Mohorovicic discontinuity
 d. Outer core

List-II
 i. Relatively strong shell broken into plates
 ii. Associated with mantle flow
 iii. Boundary between crust and mantle
 iv. Liquid layer that generates the magnetic field

x: Mantle movement drives the plates, and the mantle is a major source of magma. The other options deny one of these roles.
t: Recall the role of the mantle.

x: P-waves are primary waves, S-waves secondary waves and surface waves L-waves, while a seismograph records them, giving a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Recall each wave's alternative name.
s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding seismic waves.

List-I
 a. P-waves
 b. S-waves
 c. Surface waves
 d. Seismograph

List-II
 i. Secondary waves
 ii. L-waves
 iii. Primary waves
 iv. Instrument that records seismic waves

x: Both are true: a volcano is an outlet for magma, lava and gases, and surface waves are also called L-waves (long waves).
t: Check each statement separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A volcano is an outlet for magma, lava and gases.
Statement B: Surface waves are also called L-waves.

x: All five are correct: P-waves are fastest and arrive first, S-waves are slower, and surface waves are slowest.
t: Arrange seismic waves by speed.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. S-waves are slower than P-waves.
II. Surface waves are the slowest seismic waves.
III. S-waves do not arrive first.
IV. Surface waves do not arrive first.
V. P-waves are faster than S-waves.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: All four are correct: P-waves cross solids, liquids and gases, S-waves only solids, and surface waves travel only along the surface.
t: Recall the medium each wave can cross.
s:
Consider the following statements about the media through which seismic waves travel:
I. P-waves travel through solids, liquids and gases.
II. S-waves travel through solids but do not travel through gases.
III. Surface waves travel through solids.
IV. P-waves and S-waves travel through Earth's interior, whereas surface waves do not travel through Earth's interior.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: P-waves vibrate along their direction (push–pull), and S-waves vibrate across it (shear).
t: Discriminate longitudinal from transverse waves.

x: S-waves are slower than P-waves, P-waves refract strongly at the mantle–core boundary, the Gutenberg discontinuity separates mantle and outer core, and S-waves vanishing proves the outer core is liquid, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Relate wave behaviour to the outer core.
s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding seismic waves and the outer core.

List-I
 a. S-waves
 b. P-waves at the mantle–core boundary
 c. Gutenberg discontinuity
 d. Disappearance of S-waves

List-II
 i. Strong refraction
 ii. Establishes that the outer core is liquid
 iii. Slower than P-waves
 iv. Boundary between the mantle and the outer core

x: Both are true: the P-wave shadow zone is about 105°–140°, and S-waves never reappear beyond about 105°.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All six are correct: earthquake waves change speed in different materials, reflect and refract, and their shadow zones reveal internal boundaries.
t: Recall how seismic waves reveal the interior.

x: All six are correct: the interior has crust, mantle and core; a velocity jump marks the Moho, S-waves vanishing and P-waves changing speed mark the Gutenberg, and the Lehmann marks the inner core.
t: Recall the seismic clue for each boundary.
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Earth’s internal structure includes the crust, mantle and core.
II. A sudden velocity increase is the seismic clue for the Mohorovicic discontinuity.
III. The disappearance of S-waves is a seismic clue for the Gutenberg discontinuity.
IV. P-wave velocity change is a seismic clue for the Gutenberg discontinuity.
V. The Lehmann discontinuity is linked to the solid inner core.
VI. Crustal velocity change is the seismic clue for the Conrad discontinuity.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: the 410 km and 660 km discontinuities mark mineral phase changes in the mantle.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All four are correct: Earth averages about 5.5 g/cm³, is the densest planet, and grows denser inward with heavy materials in the core.
t: Recall the facts of Earth's density.

x: Both are true and R explains A: internal heat drives processes within Earth, which is what endogenic means.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: R describes what mantle dynamics then cause, not why endogenic processes produce them.
t: Check whether R is the cause or a result.

x: All three are correct: plate movement causes folding, faulting, earthquakes, volcanism and mountain building.
t: Recall the effects of plate movement.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Plate movement produces folding and faulting.
II. Plate movement produces earthquakes and volcanism.
III. Plate movement produces mountain building.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: All three are correct: mantle heat drives convection, the asthenosphere lets plates move, and the lithosphere is broken into plates.
t: Recall the mechanism of plate movement.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Mantle heat produces convection or thermal movement.
II. The asthenosphere allows lithospheric plates to move.
III. The lithosphere is broken into plates.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Igneous rocks form from cooling magma or lava, sedimentary rocks from deposition, metamorphic rocks from heat and pressure, and granite is intrusive while basalt is extrusive, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall how each rock type forms.

x: Magma produces volcanism, the mantle lies below the crust, a volcano releases lava, ash and gases and water vapour is the most abundant volcanic gas, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the features of volcanism.

x: The outer core is mainly liquid iron and nickel. Silicates belong to the mantle and O–Si–Al–Fe to the crust.
t: Recall the composition of each layer.

x: The asthenosphere is mechanically weak and ductile, which is why plates can slide over it.
t: Discriminate lithosphere from asthenosphere.

x: Option D is incorrect: surface waves, not P-waves, are the most destructive. P-waves are fastest and S-waves slower than them.
t: Separate the fastest wave from the most destructive one.
o: P-waves are the fastest seismic waves.
Surface waves have the highest destructive power.
P-waves have higher destructive power than surface waves.

x: Both are true: molten rock below the surface is magma, and once it reaches the surface it is lava.
t: Discriminate magma from lava.
